correctness.rationale: For the stated real hexagonal norm, the source reduces Fu–Li’s unit-sphere quotient to an exact range optimization. Simultaneous coordinate permutations and q↦1/q exhaust all pairs. For the identity case |r−s|≤rng(0,qr−s,q−1); reversal gives 2√q/(1+q)≤√q(2−q). For either transposition the maximum of (x+y)/(qx+max(1−q,y)) is 2−q; for either cycle the maximum of (1+m)/max(q+m,1+qx) at fixed m reduces to the two boundary choices and is ≤2−q. Hence R≤√q(2−q), squared deficit (8−3q)(3q−2)^2/27≥0. Explicit u=(0,1), v=(1,2/3), a=√(2/3) attains 32/27 squared. Direct six-case numerical optimization and exact rational identity checks corroborate, not replace, the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The affine-regular hexagonal plane is a canonical natural polygonal Banach model; DR is a motivated angular-versus-skew angular distortion invariant. The attained exact value √(32/27) gives a nontrivial benchmark strictly between Hilbert 1 and square/diamond 2, rather than an arbitrary slice of a known table. The symmetry-reduced finite-case analytic optimization is reusable for other polygonal norms, although no such generalization is claimed.
